sentences.text:
Debarun Das vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 9 July, 2025
Item 09.07.

In The High Court At Calcutta
 No. 2025 Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side
 01
Ct 32 Crr 3595 of 2024
 With
rup Ia No: Cran 1 of 2024
 Debarun Das
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Anr.
 Mr. Rajeshwar Chakraborty.
 Mr. Subhrajit Dey,
 ... for the petitioner.
 Mr. Navanil De,
 Ms. Monami Mukherjee. ... for the O.P. No.2.
 Ms. Amita Gaur. ... for the State.

1.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties to this revisional application are present.
2. One report has been submitted on behalf of the State in compliance with the order dated 30.06.2025 and the same be kept with the record.

3. One joint petition has been filed by the petitioner and the opposite party No.2 with a prayer for quashing the proceeding which is impugned in this revisional application as parties have already arrived at settlement.

4. From the report submitted on behalf of the State, it is also found that the de facto complainant is also not willing to proceed with the case, which was investigated and ended in chargesheet under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
5. Considering all facts and circumstances, further proceeding with the case would be a glaring example of abuse of process of court.
6. In the aforesaid view of the matter, prayer of joint petition (CRAN 1 of 2024) stands allowed.
